title: The dual category of local transversal strings is braided tensor equivalent to the representation category of the quantum double
author: Shiyu Cao, Zhian Jia and Sheng Tan
work: Topological quantum color code model on infinite lattice
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 3.22 of the article (source label thm:category_equivalence, source0.tex lines 1553--1555), which the article itself calls the main result of the paper: the category $\mathcal D_{\rm loc,tr}^{\rm dual}$ is braided tensor equivalent to the representation category $\Rep(D(\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2))$. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 52-line proof at source0.tex lines 1558--1609. H2: the proof is a full computation of a braided tensor equivalence rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must set up the eight irreducible representations of the quantum double of $G=\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ labelled by pairs $(g,\chi)$, identify the four flux-charge composites of the color code with those simples, construct the fusion rules and the $R$-matrices, compute the topological $S$- and $T$-matrices of the color code model in the infinite-lattice limit and compare them with the modular data of $D(G)$, and finally verify the braiding and the tensor structure on morphisms. Reproducing that equivalence between a topological stabilizer model and a quantum double is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
